children: The global oil market is expected to return to a surplus in Q4 for the first time since the Iran war began, as exports from the Middle Eastern recover faster than global demand despite continued attacks on shipping, the International Energy Agency said Friday in its latest monthly report.

Global oil supply rose by 2.3M bbl/day in October to 105.4M bbl/day, following a 3M bbl/day increase in September, as Persian Gulf exports "recovered much faster than global oil demand," with shipments from the region, excluding Oman, reaching 18.4M bbl/day in October, 26% below pre-war levels, the IEA reported.

The increase prompted the agency to raise its Q4 global supply estimate by 3.3M bbl/day, while projecting a larger market surplus in 2027, but it warned that further attacks on shipping could undermine the recovery.

The IEA said it expects global oil supply to decline by 4.8M bbl/day in 2026 before rebounding by 6.6M bbl/day to an average of 108.1M bbl/day next year, while global oil demand is forecast to fall by 2.7M bbl/day in 2026 to 102.3M bbl/day, with demand recovering by 2M bbl/day in 2027, as growth begins to resume around March.

IEA member countries plan to release another 71M barrels of emergency oil stocks through February 2027, equivalent to ~600K bbl/day over the period, which would bring the total volume of emergency stocks released since March to 420M barrels, exceeding the 400M barrels initially committed by IEA countries.

The recovery in Gulf exports has helped push crude prices lower, with North Sea Dated crude falling more than 30% from a high of $136/bbl in early October to ~$93/bbl when the report was prepared; European diesel prices fell 11% over the same period but remained 77% above pre-war levels.
Crude oil futures ended mixed Friday but both WTI and Brent posted a second straight weekly decline, as the market remains edgy about the continuing Middle East conflict and the next move by the U.S.
